I'm gathering evidence for two new Zimmermann PWA Kit stories before any code is written (a pre-build readiness gate — you are read-only, do not write or edit anything):

- SFCC-801: a reusable `global/country-currency-selector` React component — a right-anchored slide-in drawer letting shoppers pick shipping country, currency, and optionally language. Consumed later by SFCC-688/SFCC-817 (redirect logic is NOT in this story's scope).
- SFCC-831: a reusable `global/country-language-mismatch` React component — also a right-anchored drawer using "the shared drawer shell", with two variants: a Location Prompt Banner (consumed by SFCC-823) and a Language Prompt Banner (consumed by SFCC-689). Trigger/redirect logic is NOT in this story's scope.

I need a thorough map of what already exists in this codebase (`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`) that's relevant, so we can plan the smallest correct build. Please investigate and report back on:

1. **Shared drawer shell**: Is there already a `ZimmDrawer` (or similarly named) atom/component under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`? I have prior evidence (from `.claude/rules/testing.md` and other rules files) that a `zimmDrawer` component exists with variants like a "Large" story and portal-rendered content. Find its exact path, read its props/API (index.tsx), its recipe file, and its Storybook story to understand what sizes/variants it already supports (mobile/tablet/desktop) and whether it's suitable as the shell for both new components.
2. **Any existing locale/region/country/currency selector work**: grep for `countryCurrency`, `country-currency`, `localeSelector`, `regionSelector`, `CurrencySelector`, `LanguageSelector`, `countryLanguageMismatch`, `locationPrompt`, `languagePrompt`, `geoRedirect`, `ipCountry` etc. across `overrides/`. I recall from project memory that a "locale selector" was previously a dead end blocked on an "unbuilt region selector" and that footer country label isn't derivable from config — check if that's still true, and whether either of these two new stories IS that previously-missing region selector.
3. **`overrides/app/config/countries.ts`**: read it — what shape is country/currency/language config in today? Does it have enough data (currency codes, language options per country) to drive a selector UI, or would this story need new config?
4. **`use-multi-site.ts`** and **`use-navigation.ts`** hooks (Tier 1, `overrides/app/hooks/`) — read them and summarize what site/locale switching capability already exists at the hook level, since a country/currency/language selector will need to call into something like this to actually change site context. Don't suggest modifying these files (they're frozen) — just report their current API surface.
5. **Existing organisms that compose a drawer + form controls** (e.g. `zimmSubscribeSection`, `zimmSubscribeModal`, any cart/wishlist drawer) — find one or two of the closest existing patterns for "organism that owns a drawer, holds local state, and calls callback props" so we know which exemplar to build from.
6. **Tier check**: using `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` (NOT `.claude/registry/*.md`, which is known to have a wrong/unreliable Tier column), determine what tier a new `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCountryCurrencySelector/` (or similar) and `zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/` folder would fall under, and whether `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` (which may need new fields) is Tier 1 (it's listed under "Runtime & Integration Config" in frozenFiles.md — confirm).
7. Check `CODEOWNERS` for who owns `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**` and `overrides/app/config/**`.

Report concrete file paths and line numbers/snippets, not summaries without evidence. Note explicitly anything you searched for and did NOT find (absence is itself a finding here). Keep the report well-organized under the 7 numbered headings above, and be thorough — this feeds a go/no-go build-readiness decision.

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- zimmerMANNBuild: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
- zimmerMANNDevImprover: Looks back over completed build work and improves the build chain. Reads the session transcripts and run artefacts for named stories, diagnoses where the loop failed and whose gap it was, checks whether the skills still cite things that are true, and proposes concrete edits to the build skills and loop agents — applied only on Marcel's explicit go.
- zimmerMANNDevOps: Runs deploys, promotions across environments, tags, release cuts and rollbacks on the Zimmermann PWA Kit. Verifies pipeline state live before every action, shows what each environment is running, and executes only on explicit approval. Reports broken gates and stops rather than working around them.
- zimmerMANNPostBuild: The senior dev pass after a build. Audits what zimmerMANNBuild produced against zimmerMANNPreBuild's plan and findings, runs a whole-feature sweep for uniform defects, writes the PR body, and owns the review conversation — pushing and replying only on Marcel's go.
- zimmerMANNPreBuild: The gate and planner before any Zimmermann PWA Kit build work. Gathers and cross-checks every source — Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase and Figma — flags every gap and misalignment, then produces an executable closed-loop build plan and hands off to zimmerMANNBuild. Use at the start of any story, ticket or build task.
- zimmerMANNReview: Reviews someone else's PR as FED Lead. Establishes ground truth, fans out audit angles, verifies every finding before it is raised, then presents for adjudication — Marcel decides the verdict, and comments post only on his go. Loops until the PR is approved.
- zimmerMANNRevImprover: Looks back over completed PR reviews and improves how Marcel reviews. Reads the PR outcome and the review session transcript to judge whether each finding held up, whether anything was missed, and how the review was actually conducted — then proposes concrete edits to zimmerMANNReview, applied only on his explicit go.
- zimmerMANNSprinter: The skill for sprint and agile ceremonies as FED Lead — backlog refinement, sprint planning, standups, retros, and prep for any meeting. Reads Jira and Confluence, drafts what you need to take into the room, and writes to Jira only on your explicit go.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
- upstream-sync-review: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- feature-dev:feature-dev: Guided feature development with codebase understanding and architecture focus
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- commit-commands:clean_gone: Cleans up all git branches marked as [gone] (branches that have been deleted on the remote but still exist locally), including removing associated worktrees.
- commit-commands:commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR
- commit-commands:commit: Create a git commit
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- pr-review-toolkit:review-pr: Comprehensive PR review using specialized agents
- agent-sdk-dev:new-sdk-app: Create and setup a new Claude Agent SDK application
- plugin-dev:create-plugin: Guided end-to-end plugin creation workflow with component design, implementation, and validation
- vercel:bootstrap: Bootstrap a repository with Vercel-linked resources by running preflight checks, provisioning integrations, verifying env keys, and then executing db/dev startup commands safely.
- vercel:deploy: Deploy the current project to Vercel. Pass "prod" or "production" as argument to deploy to production. Default is preview deployment.
- vercel:env: Manage Vercel environment variables. Commands include list, pull, add, remove, and diff. Use to sync environment variables between Vercel and your local development environment.
- vercel:status: Show the status of the current Vercel project — recent deployments, linked project info, and environment overview.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers a dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. 116	      justifyContent: 'center',

132	      minWidth: 0,

Search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the redirect — match by User-Agent against a comprehensive allowlist (Googlebot incl. # SFCC Business Manager ↔ PWA Kit Region/Locale Sync — Findings & Implementation

## Context

Zimmermann's storefront config (which SFCC sites exist, what locales/currencies each
serves, what URL prefix each uses) originates in Salesforce Business Manager (BM) but has
to be manually re-created inside this PWA Kit repo for the storefront to route and render
each region correctly. This document started as investigation into how that sync worked
and where it was fragile, then became the design + implementation record once the SCAPI
sync option (formerly "Option A" below) was actually built out. **Status: implemented and
locally testing as of this update** — see "What's actually built" below. The known
7-vs-8-storefront count drift (US domestic/international split, per
`.docs/prd/regional.md` REG-005) is a separate, smaller fix and deliberately not detailed
here — it's easy and will be picked up on its own later.

## How sync worked before this PR — five hand-maintained locations, and this is Salesforce's documented pattern

BM config was manually transcribed into five locations (six files, two of which are
grouped pairs) that had to stay in lockstep: `.docs/prd/regional.md` (requirements source
of truth); `config/sites.js` + `config/default.js` together (the config PWA Kit actually
runs on — **Tier 1**); `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` (a second, independent config
keyed by URL slug — **Tier 1**); `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts` (SFCC↔Contentful
mapping); and `e2e/fixtures/site.js` + `customers.js` together (Playwright fixtures). See
"What's actually built" below for how this looks now — `sites.js`/`default.js` are joined
by `sites.generated.js`/`sites.overlay.js`, and `countries.ts`/`contentfulMapping.ts`/the
e2e fixtures each gained their own generated + overlay split too.

This is not a Zimmermann anti-pattern — Salesforce's own docs confirm `config/sites.js`
exists specifically to be manually kept in sync with Business Manager, and that
`l10n.supportedLocales` "must match" BM's locale settings, by design. Salesforce's newer
"Storefront Next" template consolidates this to one file (`config.server.ts`'s
`commerce.sites`) plus an env-var override, but even there `i18n.supportedLngs` still has
to be manually kept aligned with `commerce.sites[].supportedLocales` — the sync surface
shrinks, but a fully single-source-of-truth config doesn't exist anywhere Salesforce
documents, current or next-gen.

The one file that actually determines whether a region loads correctly at runtime is
`config/sites.js`: `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` (`AppConfig.restore`)
resolves site+locale per request by scanning every site's `l10n.supportedLocales` for a
match against the URL's locale segment, and **falls back silently to the AU default site
if nothing matches — no error, no log**. Everything else (`countries.ts`,
`contentfulMapping.ts`, e2e fixtures) is a secondary mirror of whatever `sites.js` says.

## Option A — a SCAPI sync job to replace part of the manual transcription

OCAPI (the old Data API path for reading site config) is officially deprecated (April
2026, ~2-year patch-only tail). The relevant current SCAPI endpoint is confirmed:

- **`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/configurations?siteId={siteId}`**
  (`configuration/shopper-configurations/v1`, confirmed via
  `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s generated types — this is a real, typed client
  method already available in a dependency this repo has, not a new package).
- Returns a `siteConfiguration` entry covering **name, status, currencies, and locales**
  per site — exactly what `config/sites.js` needs to stay correct.
- **Uses the same SLAS shopper credentials already used elsewhere in this repo.** This is
  materially better than it first looked — the initially-found `sfcc.preferences`/`sfcc.sites`
  Admin APIs would have needed a brand-new Account Manager client_credentials setup;
  Shopper Configurations needs no new credential class at all.
- **One call per site — there's no org-wide "list all sites" call.** A sync script needs
  to already know the site ID list (which it does — it's the thing being verified).
- Explicitly documented as "highly cacheable" — this is designed for infrequent polling,
  not a per-request call. **Confirms the user's instinct: this should be a sync job run on
  demand or on a schedule (e.g. a `scripts/sfcc/` script analogous to
  `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs`, run manually before a release or on a cron),
  never called at runtime from the storefront itself.**

**What this closes, and what it doesn't:** a sync job here can _verify_ `config/sites.js`
against live BM (site status, locales, currencies) and flag drift — but it can't safely
_auto-write_ `config/sites.js`, since that file is Tier 1 and any write still needs
Integration-team review. Realistic shape: a `detect:regional-drift`-style script that
exits non-zero and prints a diff when BM and `config/sites.js` disagree, run manually or
in CI, not an auto-fix. This directly addresses the "5 files, easy to miss one" concern —
it wouldn't eliminate the files, but it would catch drift in the most important one
(`config/sites.js`) without hand-comparing against a BM screenshot.

**Update: built, and taken further than originally scoped here** — see "What's actually
built" below. Rather than a read-only drift-checker, the user (a verified
`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` member) opted to have the script actually write the
derived config, extended to all four hand-maintained files, not just `config/sites.js`.

## 1. Shared drawer shell — `ZimmDrawer`

Confirmed at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/`:
- `index.tsx` (233 lines) — component + `ZimmDrawerContent` internal

- `index.stories.tsx` (128 lines)

**Props/API** (`index.tsx` lines 37–75):
```ts
export type ZimmDrawerSize = 'large' | 'tablet' | 'small' | 'xLarge' | 'mobile';
type ZimmDrawerBaseProps = {
  isOpen: boolean;
  onClose: () => void;
  size: ZimmDrawerSize;
  children: React.ReactNode;
  titleStyle?: 'large' | 'small';          // default 'large'
  finalFocusRef?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement>;
  initialFocusRef?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement>;
};
// discriminated union — exactly one of:
type ZimmDrawerProps = ZimmDrawerBaseProps & (
  | { title: string; labelledBy?: never; 'aria-label'?: never }
  | { title?: never; labelledBy: string; 'aria-label'?: never }
  | { title?: never; labelledBy?: never; 'aria-label': string }
);
```
Built on Chakra's `Drawer` primitive with `placement="right"` hardcoded (line 206) — focus trap/restore, ESC/overlay-click-close, body-scroll lock all come from Chakra. Own `ZimmDrawerContent` replaces Chakra's `<DrawerContent>` with a `framer-motion`-driven symmetric slide (SFCC-898 fix — see the file's motion-token comments). Rendered via Chakra's Portal (confirmed in `index.stories.tsx` lines 33–36, `within(document.body)` per "testing.md §Layer-2 exception," and `.claude/rules/testing.md:136`'s citation of this exact `Large` story).

**Size variants** (`zimmDrawer.css.ts` lines 8–30, 137–199) — 5 named, Figma-matched, each collapsing to `mobile` baseStyle below the `md` breakpoint regardless of chosen size:
| Variant | Width (≥md) | Named consumers per file comment |
|---|---|---|
| `large` | 50% | Product Details, Filters (desktop) |
| `tablet` | 80% | Product Details, Filters (tablet) — graduates to `large` at desktop via caller's `useBreakpointValue` |
| `small` | 25% | **"Notify Me, Wishlist, Find in Boutique, Regional Storefront, Cookies, Login"** |
| `xLarge` | 82% | Cart (not built as a drawer yet — no consumer) |
| `mobile` | — | baseStyle only |

Notably, `zimmDrawer.css.ts` line 10 and line 24 already name **"Regional Storefront"** as a `size="small"` consumer alongside Wishlist/Login — i.e., this shell was already designed anticipating a country/region drawer of this shape. Stories confirm all 5 sizes (`Large`/`Tablet`/`Small`/`XLarge`/`Mobile`), both title modes (`WithTitleLarge`/`WithTitleSmallStyle`/`WithTitleSmallDrawer`), and close-button behavior (`CloseButtonClosesTheDrawer`/`TitleCloseButtonClosesTheDrawer`).

**Verdict: suitable as-is as the shell for both SFCC-801 and SFCC-831.** No changes to `ZimmDrawer` itself appear necessary — `title` mode handles a simple header, `labelledBy` mode is available if either drawer needs a custom header (e.g., two-CTA banner layout for the mismatch prompts).

Current consumers: `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` (`size="small"`, `title` mode) and `ZimmPdpDrawer` (dynamic size, `labelledBy` mode via its own tab header) — see §5.

## 2. Existing locale/region/country/currency selector work

**Not found anywhere in `overrides/`:** `zimmCountryCurrencySelector`, `zimmCountryLanguageMismatch`, `zimmRegionSelector`, `zimmLocaleSelector`, `ZimmRegion*`, `ZimmCountry*`, `ZimmCurrency*`, `ZimmLanguage*`, `shippingDrawer`, `storefrontSelector`, `geoRedirect`, `ipCountry`, `locationPrompt`, `languagePrompt`. Two independent broad greps across `overrides/` (by keyword, and by filename pattern for `*country*|*currency*|*locale*|*region*`) turned up nothing beyond what's discussed below. Confirmed empty: no `zimmCountryCurrencySelector/` or `zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/` directory anywhere under `ui-kits/atoms|molecules|organisms`.

**`LocaleSelector` exists only as the stock upstream component**, never overridden:
- `.claude/registry/components.md:37` — `Base | app/components/locale-selector/index.jsx | locales: array, selectedLocale: string`
- Source (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/locale-selector/index.jsx`): an `Accordion` disclosure with hardcoded flag icons for only `en-GB/fr-FR/it-IT/zh-CN/ja-JP` — doesn't cover Zimmermann's 11-locale set at all.
- **Direct evidence it was explicitly trimmed out of the mobile drawer menu** — `overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/index.test.tsx:38-42`:
  > "No ZimmIcon/LocaleSelector/SocialIcons mocks needed — the mobile drawer's L1/L2 content (index.tsx) doesn't import any of them: the account/store-locator/locale/support/social sections and the chevron affordance were all trimmed to match Figma's 'Expanded Menu' frame (plain-text L1 rows, Wishlist/Account footer only)."

  This directly confirms the mobile hamburger placement PRD calls for (`.docs/prd/homepage.md:38`, HPC-025 — "country/region selector is also surfaced within the mobile hamburger/burger menu") is **not implemented today** — it was cut from `drawer-menu`'s build.

**Header/footer have no trigger stub either.** `grep` of `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`, `leftBar/index.tsx`, `rightBar/index.tsx` for `region|country|currency|locale` returns zero matches. `.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md` repeatedly defers this (lines 605, 726, 855, 1186, 1425), e.g. line 1425: "**Carried forward, not solved here:** header region selector (needs its own Figma + Integration-lead sign-off)."

**Footer's only "country" hit is unrelated**: `overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.content.ts:67` — "Acknowledgement of Country" (Indigenous land-acknowledgement link label), not a selector.

**PRD ground truth exists and maps cleanly onto the two stories** (`.docs/prd/regional.md` §2):
- REG-014–019: country-mismatch "slide-out," shown first-visit only if IP country ≠ storefront region; two CTAs (redirect / open country selector); bag-loss warning → **SFCC-831's Location Prompt Banner**.
- REG-020–024: "Country + language selector," all storefronts except AU, countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with currency display + search field; EU domestic offers EN/FR/IT/ES, others English-only → **SFCC-801**.
- REG-029–035: EU-only language-mismatch modal (IP country ≠ URL language), two CTAs (continue/switch), explicit country→language map → **SFCC-831's Language Prompt Banner**.
- `.docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md:45` (PRC-14): "Country/currency selector shows prices in the currency configured for the customer's selected shipping country... the country selector is not present on the AU site."

**On the user's recalled claim** ("locale selector was a dead end blocked on an unbuilt region selector"; "footer country label isn't derivable from config"): I could **not find this stated verbatim** anywhere searched — `.claude/rules/*`, `.claude/registry/*`, all 5 files in `.docs/memory/` (`feedback.md`, `projectState.md`, `references.md`, `sprintScope.md`, `upstreamBaseline.md`), `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, full git log (`--all --grep`, case-insensitive on all relevant terms), and `git branch -a`. This should be treated as **unconfirmed by the repo** — likely a prior verbal/session recollection not persisted to files. That said, the circumstantial evidence above (drawer-menu's explicit trim, SFCC-52's repeated deferrals, zero header code, and — per §3 below — the `region` Contentful content type's `label` field being explicitly documented as "not shopper-facing copy") is consistent with the spirit of the claim even without the exact sentence.

**Does either new story appear to BE the previously-missing region selector?** SFCC-801 substantially overlaps with the "header region selector" that SFCC-52 explicitly deferred (REG-020–024). SFCC-831 is a related but distinct PRD concept (mismatch prompt banners, REG-014–019/029–035) rather than the persistent selector itself. Both stories explicitly exclude trigger/redirect logic, so building them does not by itself wire up the header/footer/mobile-menu entry points or the geo-IP mismatch trigger — that remains separate downstream work (presumably SFCC-688/817/823/689).

## 3. `overrides/app/config/countries.ts`

Read in full (129 lines). Shape:
```ts
export type CountryConfig = {
  urlSlug: string; sfccSiteId: string; locale: string; currency: string; // ISO 4217
  shippingCountry: string;      // ISO 3166-1 alpha-2
  checkoutOwner: 'sfcc' | 'global-e' | 'hybrid';
  globalEPricing: boolean;
  boutiqueRegion: string;       // key for store-locator filtering only
};
export const COUNTRIES: Record<string, CountryConfig>;   // 11 entries
export const DEFAULT_COUNTRY_SLUG = 'au';
export const COUNTRY_BY_SHIPPING_CODE: Record<string, CountryConfig>; // "used by IP-detection prompt" (line 125)
```
`sfccSiteId`/`locale`/`currency` are SCAPI-derived (`countries.generated.ts`, "do not hand-edit," regenerated via `npm run sync:regional-config`); `shippingCountry`/`checkoutOwner`/`globalEPricing`/`boutiqueRegion` are hand-maintained in `COUNTRY_OVERLAY` (lines 75–87). `COUNTRY_BY_SHIPPING_CODE`'s doc comment shows it was already built with a mismatch-detection consumer in mind — a useful existing building block for SFCC-831.

**Is there enough data to drive a selector UI? Partially — gaps exist:**
- **Has**: currency, locale, one ISO2 shipping country per storefront, and a ready-made ISO2→config reverse lookup.
- **Missing**:
  1. **No shopper-facing display names** ("Australia", "United Kingdom") — only machine codes (`urlSlug`, `sfccSiteId`, `locale`, ISO codes).
  2. **No region-grouping** (REG-021 needs "Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas" buckets). `boutiqueRegion` is a different, narrower concept — only 6 flat keys (`australia/usa/uk/europe/hong-kong/middle-east`) for store-locator filtering (line 56), not a 3-bucket selector grouping.
  3. **No per-country language-options list** — EU's 4 languages exist only as 4 separate top-level `COUNTRIES` slugs (`en-eu/fr-eu/it-eu/es-eu`), not as "one France entry + a language sub-list" a selector would want.
  4. **No full destination-country list** — `regional.md` §1 enumerates ~150 individual countries mapped to the 8 storefronts, but that only exists as PRD prose, not code; `countries.ts` only has 11 storefront-level entries with one `shippingCountry` each.
  5. The only other "region" concept in the repo, the Contentful `region` content type (`scripts/contentful/content-types/region.js`), is explicitly non-shopper-facing: its `label` field comment (lines 22–29) reads *"Editor-facing display name... Admin label, not shopper-facing copy — not localized."*
- **Confirmed per user's suspicion**: `countries.generated.ts`'s SCAPI source (per `.docs/planning/regionalConfigSyncPlan.md`, "Shopper Configurations" endpoint) returns only "name, status, currencies, and locales" — no display-name/region-grouping data exists upstream to sync in, either.

**Conclusion**: building either selector likely needs new fields on `CountryConfig` (display name, region group, language options) — which means touching the Tier 1 file — or a separate non-Tier-1 data source owned by the new component itself. This is a real planning fork; see §6.

## 4. `use-multi-site.ts` and `use-navigation.ts`

**Critical finding: neither file exists in `overrides/app/hooks/` today.** Full directory listing of `overrides/app/hooks/` (30 files) shows only Zimmermann-authored camelCase hooks (`useCountryConfig.ts`, `useZimmModal.ts`, etc.) plus one kebab-case file, `use-modal-state.ts`. There is no `use-multi-site.ts`, `use-navigation.ts`, `use-current-basket.ts`, `use-currency.ts`, `use-auth-modal.ts`, etc., despite all being named in `frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md`/`CODEOWNERS`.

This is explained by the project's extensibility model — `package.json`: `"extends": "@salesforce/retail-react-app", "overridesDir": "overrides"`. A path only needs a file under `overrides/app/...` once Zimmermann customizes it; until then the app transparently uses the stock file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/...`. `frozenFiles.md:65` ("the hooks above are the overrides surface") pre-declares governance for *if/when* an override is created — it doesn't assert one exists yet. **Today's actual hook-level API is the unmodified upstream implementation**, read directly from `node_modules`:

```js
// node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site.js
const useMultiSite = () => {
    const context = useContext(MultiSiteContext)   // throws if no MultiSiteProvider
    const {buildUrl: originalFn, site, locale} = context
    const buildUrl = useCallback((path, siteRef, localeRef) =>
        originalFn(path, siteRef ?? site?.alias ?? site?.id, localeRef ?? locale?.alias ?? locale?.id),
        [originalFn, site, locale])
    return {site, locale, buildUrl}
}
```
```js
// node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-navigation.js
const useNavigation = () => {
    const {site, locale, buildUrl} = useMultiSite()
    return useCallback((path, action='push', ...args) => {
        const updatedHref = buildUrl(removeSiteLocaleFromPath(path))
        history[action](path === '/' ? '/' : updatedHref, ...args)
    }, [locale, site])
}
```
Key API-surface facts for planning:
- `useMultiSite()` returns the **current** `site`/`locale`/`buildUrl`. `buildUrl(path, siteRef?, localeRef?)` is the only mechanism to construct a URL for a *different* site/locale — pass an explicit target ref to get a cross-storefront URL.
- `useNavigation()` always navigates using the **current** site/locale (not a caller-supplied target) and special-cases `path === '/'` to skip the prefix entirely — a footnote worth knowing: `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx` lines 188–192 explicitly avoids `useNavigation` for its own site-switch-adjacent logo link for exactly this reason, using `buildUrl` + `history.push` directly instead.
- **Neither hook exposes a mutator to switch the active site/locale** — there is no `setSite`/`setLocale`. Switching sites is done purely by navigating to a URL built for a different site/locale (site/locale is resolved server-side per-request from the URL by `_app-config`'s `AppConfig.restore`, per `.docs/planning/regionalConfigSyncPlan.md`). So a selector's "Apply" action fundamentally means: build a target URL via `buildUrl(path, newSiteRef, newLocaleRef)`, then `history.push`/full navigation — mirroring the footer's own precedent.
- `useCountryConfig()` (`overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts`, Zimmermann-authored, **no CODEOWNERS/Tier entry at all**) is the existing convenience layer that turns `useMultiSite()`'s raw `site`/`locale` into a full `CountryConfig` — already the documented precedent for "read current region state" (cited explicitly in `footer/index.tsx:195`). This is the natural hook a new selector reads FROM.
- Adjacent, not asked but relevant: `use-currency.ts` is also Tier 2 (`protectedFiles.md:88`, `CODEOWNERS:130`) and **also doesn't exist as an override yet** — same stock-upstream situation, relevant if either selector needs currency formatting.

## 5. Closest existing organism exemplars (drawer + local state + callback props)

Best match — **`ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer`** (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx`, 96 lines) + **`useWishlistAuthDrawer`** (`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, 331 lines):

- This is the strongest structural precedent for "organism owns a drawer, holds state, calls callback props": component stays presentational, all state/effects/SDK calls live in a co-located `use*.ts` hook, parent-facing callback is a single prop (`onAuthSuccess?: () => void`). Files present: `index.tsx`, `index.stories.tsx` (Storybook title `'Commerce/ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer'`), `index.test.tsx`.

Also useful:
- **`ZimmPdpDrawer`** (`organisms/zimmPdpDrawer/index.tsx`, 80 lines) — simpler organism directly on `ZimmDrawer`, genuinely local `useState` (no extracted hook) for `activeTabId`; uses `labelledBy` mode (its own `ZimmTabs` header) instead of `ZimmDrawer`'s built-in `title`. Good precedent when state is simple enough to stay inline.
- **`ZimmSubscribeModal`** (`organisms/zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx`, 104 lines) — best reference specifically for the "form controls + callback props" half (`onSubmit(firstName, lastName)`, `onClose`), though built on `ZimmModal`, not `ZimmDrawer`. Shows the uncontrolled-form-via-`form.elements.namedItem` convention and Cancel/Continue button-row layout.
- **`zimmSubscribeSection`** (`organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx`) + `useSubscribeSection.ts` — same organism+hook split, applied to an inline (non-drawer) form; a third data point for the pattern.

Recommendation basis (not a build instruction, just what the evidence supports): given both new components need meaningfully more state than `ZimmPdpDrawer`'s single `useState`, and SFCC-831 needs two variants, `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` + `useWishlistAuthDrawer`'s organism/hook split is the closer structural template of the two drawer examples.
